column1: # Narration for the demo, one line per row, pipe separated:
#   <second on the assembled timeline>|<words>
# The assembled file is three pieces: the HyperFrames explainer (0-25s), the screen recording of the
# deployed site (25-70.3s), and the HyperFrames end card (70.3-82.3s). Starts are placed against the
# page map measured from the cut by scene detection, shifted by the explainer's length:
#     0.0 -  5.0  explainer: what it is
#     5.0 - 10.5  explainer: the mechanic
#    10.5 - 15.5  explainer: the two tolerances
#    15.5 - 20.0  explainer: what is held and what is not
#    20.0 - 25.0  explainer: the proof
#    25.0 - 28.0  the landing page, still
#    28.0 - 30.8  the overview
#    30.8 - 34.8  the case list
#    34.8 - 41.8  run a case: the case and the lie size
#    41.8 - 50.8  run a case: the steps and the feed's print
#    50.8 - 56.8  run a case: the verdict
#    56.8 - 64.3  prove a price
#    64.3 - 70.3  feeds and bonds
#    70.3 - 76.3  end card: what is live
#    76.3 - 82.3  end card: where to look
# Numbers are spelled as they are spoken, there is no marketing vocabulary, and every claim is one
# the viewer can check on screen in the same shot. Only rows that begin with a digit are read.
# Length matters: this voice runs about 16 characters a second, and build_narration.sh refuses to
# build a track whose line outlasts the segment it is talking about. The rate is left at the voice's
# own pace: a slower reading is easier to follow than a sped-up one.
0.4|A feed's price decides what a loan is worth.
5.4|The bonus a liquidation pays is computed from that price.
10.9|Two sources have to agree within five per cent.
15.7|The bonus is held for five minutes. The debt is not.
20.6|Anyone can challenge. The contract decides.
25.2|The deployed site, reading the chain.
28.0|Held bonuses and decisions.
31.2|Every case, its verdict, and the bond it paid.
35.2|A case of our own, and how far the feed will lie.
42.2|First the real price, then one that is off.
51.2|The liquidation runs on that price, and the bonus is held.
57.4|Anyone may prove a print was false. The contract records the verdict.
64.6|The bond is what pays the prover when a print is caught.
71.0|Six contracts on Arbitrum Sepolia, with no owner.
76.8|The dashboard is live, and every number on it is read from the chain.
